title: Quota-aware priority broker for tier traffic with regional model-fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a single, testable component that enforces tier-based prioritization (free / paid / enterprise) while respecting per-tenant quotas and enabling graceful degradation across regions and model variants. Current behavior is fragmented: rate-limiters live in multiple services, fallback logic is ad-hoc, and regional model selection is handled downstream, causing inconsistent user experience and edge-case starvation when quotas are low.

Goals: 1) Centralize quota-aware prioritization into a lightweight broker service (Priority Broker) that sits in the smart-routing path; 2) Ensure free-tier requests are deprioritized but not starved; paid/enterprise get guaranteed shares and burst windows; 3) Support region-aware routing preferences with configurable soft-fallbacks to alternate regions and to lower-cost model variants when capacity or quota constraints demand it; 4) Provide observability and rollbacks for any policy changes.

Proposed design: Priority Broker component that receives annotated request metadata (tenant_id, tier, preferred_region, model_hint, token_estimate). It returns a routing decision: accept->route to chosen region/model, queue->place in short soft-queue with TTL, degrade->route to cheaper model or reduced-token policy, reject->immediate 429 with clear retry-after and diagnostic. Core pieces:
- Tenant credit accounts: sliding-window token credits + reserved share for enterprise tenants.
- Dynamic weights: each tier has a configurable weight and minimum guaranteed capacity; broker calculates admission probability when capacity is constrained.
- Soft-queue: short-lived in-memory queue at edge (max 200ms hold) to allow bursts without immediate rejection.
- Regional preference matrix: prefer local region unless capacity or SLA breach predicted; fallback rules can choose nearby region or model variant family (e.g., quantized or smaller architecture).
- Degradation policy: a mapping table (tier->fallback priorities) stored in config service (Console editable). E.g. free->fallback to model-x-small or stub generation; paid->fallback to quantized variant; enterprise->try multi-region then notify ops.
- Credit smoothing: when tokens are low, apply probabilistic admission to avoid clumping and to preserve fairness across tenants.

Enforcement points and integration: implement broker as sidecar or a centralized routing tier depending on deployment mode. Hosted API will use centralized broker for observability; Dedicated/Private deployments can run broker sidecar per pod to satisfy isolation. Routing engine will expose gRPC decisions consumed by edge gateway.

Observability and metrics: per-tenant and per-tier metrics: admitted_rate, queued_rate, rejected_rate, fallback_rate, avg_latency, token_consumed, p95 routing_latency. Add tracing tags: decision_reason, chosen_region, model_variant. Dashboards and per-route alarms to detect unexpected fallback spikes.

Acceptance criteria: 1) No increase in p95 request-latency >5% in hosted baseline during canary; 2) Free-tier rejection rate under synthetic overload remains predictable and matches configured target; 3) Enterprise tenants maintain >99.5% success for admitted requests within guaranteed share; 4) All policy changes applied via Console config take effect within 60s and are audited.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement feature-flagged shadow mode in routing path for 2 weeks (traffic mirrored only); 2) Gradual canary on 1% hosted traffic with monitoring and abort on thresholds; 3) Expand to 10% then 50% then full; 4) For Dedicated/Private customers, provide an opt-in sidecar release and migration docs.

Testing: unit tests for admission logic, integration tests simulating multi-tenant burst, chaos tests for region outage fallback, load test to validate queue TTL behavior.

Risks & trade-offs: centralized broker improves observability but is a single point of failure — mitigate with HA clusters and local fallback to conservative admission policy. Soft-queue introduces additional latency; keep TTL small and observable. Quota smoothing reduces instantaneous throughput for paid customers under extreme load — mitigated by reserved burst windows for enterprise.

Docs & artifacts: design spec (Confluence), policy schema for Console, API defs for routing decisions, example rollout k8s manifests.
